Description: The AI may produce less accurate recommendations for certain demographic groups
Mitigation: Train and validate on diverse patient populations and perform bias audits across age, gender and ethnicity groups
Signal of Success: Similar model performance across demographic groups

Description: Changes in patient populations or disease patterns may reduce model accuracy
Mitigation: Continuously monitor model performance and retrain using recent hospital data
Signal of Success: Accuracy remains within predefined threshold after deployment

Description: The AI may assign an incorrect triage priority, potentially delaying care for critically ill patients or over prioritising less urgent cases
Mitigation: Require clinician review of all AI recommendations and implement confidence scores
Signal of Success: Low rate of clinically significant misclassifications

Description: A model trained using data from a single hospital may not perform reliably across different Caribbean healthcare settings
Mitigation: Include Caribbean patient data during development and validation
Signal of Success: Consistent performance on local validation datasets

Description: Excessive AI alerts may cause clinicians to ignore important notifications
Mitigation: Prioritise only high-risk alerts and allow clinicians to customise notifications
Signal of Success: Reduced number of ignored alerts over time

Description: Poorly integrated AI systems may increase documentation or review tasks instead of improving efficiency
Mitigation: Integrate AI outputs directly into existing workflows and electronic records
Signal of Success: Reduced triage completion time without increasing staff burden

Description: Software failures, network outages or hardware issues may make the AI system temporarily unavailable
Mitigation: Maintain manual triage procedures and establish backup systems
Signal of Success: No interruption of patient triage during system failure

Description: Clinicians may rely too heavily on AI recommendations and overlook their own clinical judgement
Mitigation: Train staff to critically evaluate AI outputs and require human oversight
Signal of Success: Clinicians continue to override incorrect recommendations when appropriate

Description: If the AI cannot explain its recommendations, clinicians may struggle to trust or verify its decisions
Mitigation: Provide explanations for AI recommendations and confidence scores
Signal of Success: Clinician trust and understanding scores improve

Risk: Informed Consent and Patient Trust Concerns
Description: Patients may be unaware that AI is contributing to clinical decisions, reducing trust and raising ethical concerns
Mitigation: Clearly communicate how AI is used and ensure compliance with policy regulations
Signal of Success: Positive patient feedback and low complaint rates

Description: Differences in digital infrastructure and resources may prevent some hospitals from benefiting equally from AI-assisted triage
Mitigation: Provide infrastructure support and standardised deployment across regions
Signal of Success: Comparable adoption and performance across hospitals

Risk: Underserved Groups Underrepresented in Training Data
Description: Limited representation of rural, paediatric, elderly or other vulnerable groups may reduce the model's performance for these populations
Mitigation: Conduct equity audits and include rural, paediatric and vulnerable populations in datasets
Signal of Success: Reduced performance and gaps between patient groups
